title: Lesson Plan — Special Products and Factorisation (Class 10 NIOS Mathematics)
subject: Mathematics
objectives: Recall and apply the identities (a ± b)^2 = a^2 ± 2ab + b^2 and (a + b)(a − b) = a^2 − b^2.
Use (x + a)(x + b) = x^2 + (a + b)x + ab to expand and (in reverse) to factor x^2 + bx + c.
Expand (a ± b)^3 and apply the sum/difference-of-cubes identities a^3 ± b^3 = (a ± b)(a^2 ∓ ab + b^2).
Factor polynomials by pulling out the greatest common factor, by regrouping, and by splitting the middle term of a quadratic.
Recognise difference-of-squares, perfect-square trinomial and sum/difference-of-cubes patterns in factorisation problems.
prerequisites: Chapter 3 vocabulary — terms, coefficients, polynomial, degree, FOIL.
Distributive law and the laws of exponents (Chapter 2).
HCF / LCM of integers and of monomials.
materials: A4 'identity reference card' with all five core identities (one per pair)
Set of cards with binomials and trinomials for an 'expand or factor?' card sort
Worksheet handout (Worksheet — Special Products and Factorisation)
Mini-puzzle handout: 105^2 in your head (set-up for the (a + b)^2 mental-arithmetic example)

activities.description: Mental-arithmetic puzzle. Write 105^2 = ? on the board and set a 30-second silent timer. After the timer, take three guesses, then show the elegant route: 105^2 = (100 + 5)^2 = 10000 + 1000 + 25 = 11025. Promise that this is one of FIVE identities the lesson will unlock.
teacher_actions: Pose the 105^2 puzzle silently for 30 seconds.
Connect the trick to 'square of a sum' identity.

activities.description: Pair card sort. Distribute mixed cards (some are products to expand, some are polynomials to factor): (x + 5)^2, x^2 − 9, (a − b)^3, x^2 − 7x + 12, 8x^3 + 27, x^2 − 10x + 25, etc. Pairs sort into 'expand' vs 'factor' piles and tag the named identity each one suggests.
teacher_actions: Listen for which identity students associate with each card.
Pick two pairs to share their tagging before launching the Explain phase.
student_actions: Sort cards collaboratively; verbalise the pattern.
Tag any card that resists classification for later discussion.

activities.description: Direct instruction in five blocks: (i) (a ± b)^2 derivation by FOIL, with worked example (x + 5)^2 = x^2 + 10x + 25; (ii) (a + b)(a − b) and product-sum (x + a)(x + b), with mental-arithmetic application; (iii) (a ± b)^3 expansions and a^3 ± b^3 factor identities; (iv) factorisation strategy — GCF, regrouping; (v) split-the-middle-term for quadratics with a worked example (3x^2 + 11x + 6).
teacher_actions: Write each identity on the board with a short derivation.
Work three examples per block, increasing in difficulty.
Drive home the four-step factorisation order: GCF → pattern → split-the-middle → regroup.
student_actions: Take notes; replicate every worked example.
Add the five identities to a 'rules box' for quick reference.
Predict the factor pair for 12 with sum 7 before the teacher writes (3, 4).

activities.description: Application station: students work through six worksheet problems — one expansion (a − b)^2 mental-arithmetic, one (a + b)(a − b) numerical example, one factor-by-GCF, one split-the-middle, one regrouping, one difference-of-squares applied iteratively (x^4 − 1).
teacher_actions: Circulate; offer the smallest hint that unblocks a stuck student.
Collect common slips for the Evaluate phase.
Pair fast finishers with peers who need support.
student_actions: Solve individually; compare with a partner.
Self-check against a posted answer key after the first three problems.

activities.description: Exit-ticket quiz: 8 questions drawn from the chapter's question bank — at least one per identity. Students complete silently in 9 minutes; project answers; 4-minute discussion of the two items most students missed.
teacher_actions: Distribute exit-ticket; remind students it is individual.
Time the quiz strictly to 9 minutes.
Tally results; address the top two miss items.
student_actions: Self-mark and write a one-line reflection.

activities.description: Set homework: rest of the worksheet, plus one CREATE prompt — 'Construct three different factorisable polynomials of degree 4: one using only difference-of-squares, one using a sum-of-cubes pattern combined with a common factor, and one using both regrouping and difference-of-squares.' Preview the next chapter (Linear Equations) by writing 3x − 5 = 0 and noting that finding zeros — what we just did via factoring — IS solving an equation.
teacher_actions: Announce homework due date and the CREATE prompt.
Bridge to the next chapter with the linear-equation example.
student_actions: Pack the worksheet and identity reference card.

homework: Complete the remaining problems on the Worksheet — Special Products and Factorisation handout.
Construct three factorisable polynomials of degree 4 using three different combinations of techniques; show each factorisation.
Use the identity (a + b)(a − b) = a^2 − b^2 to compute three numerical products mentally (e.g. 999 × 1001, 78 × 82, 55 × 45).
assessment_ideas: Use the 8-item exit ticket as a quick formative check.
Set a 12-question quiz drawn from the chapter's question bank for the next class as a summative assessment.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on factoring 12x^2 + 11x − 5 using the auto-grade rubric — verify split-the-middle is shown and result is verified by re-multiplying.
Run a 5-minute peer-grading round on the CREATE homework using a two-criterion rubric (correct factorisation? techniques explicitly identified?).
references: NIOS Secondary Mathematics, Module 1, Lesson 4: Special Products and Factorisation.
NCERT Class 9 Mathematics, Chapter 2: Polynomials (for the prerequisite identity background).
